title: Lyra Therapeutics - Escalation Postmortem & Next Steps
summary: Follow-up postmortem call after this week's production outage impacting realtime chat routing. Reviewed timeline, root cause (KV cache invalidation + canary deploy), mitigations deployed, and reliability improvements (observability, rollout policy updates, fallback model). Agreed next steps: run end-to-end benchmark, share audit of canary rollout config, add SLO monitoring alerts, and schedule a 2-week POC for dedicated capacity for critical endpoints.

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-16
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE); Priya Shah (Redwood SE); Luis Romero (Redwood CSM); Evan Miller (Lyra VP Eng); Sara Cho (Lyra SRE); Marcus Li (Lyra Security); Tina Park (Lyra Product); Alex Gomez (Lyra Infra)

Summary (auto): Follow-up on 2026-11-13 outage affecting realtime chat. Root cause: KV cache invalidation surfaced on canary rollback causing increased latency and model fallback thrash. Actions taken: hotfix to stabilize cache, temporary routing to fallback model, adjusted canary policy. Next steps: audit, benchmarks, pilot Dedicated for critical endpoints.

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for carving out time, we'll keep this tight. quick roll call?
[00:10] Evan (Lyra): Evan here.
[00:12] Sara (Lyra): Sara here.
[00:14] Marcus (Lyra): Marcus here.
[00:16] Jordan: Priya?
[00:17] Priya (Redwood SE): Priya on the call. Luis?
[00:19] Luis (CSM): Luis here.
[00:21] Alex (Lyra): Alex here.
[00:22] Tina (Lyra): Tina here.
[00:25] Jordan: Great. quick readout of timeline from our side then open to you and then we'll go through fix and mitigations. Priya, do the honors.
[00:30] Priya: sure. On Friday 11/13 at ~02:12 UTC we started to see increased latencies on the chat route for user-facing requests. The initial spike was small but by 02:18 it escalated - p99 latency climbed from 220ms to 2.1s, errors increased as KV cache misses caused repeated model cold starts. By 02:25 the canary rollback triggered. Unfortunately the rollback path hit a bug in cache invalidation logic which caused a resharding event and further thrashed the KV layer. That created a feedback loop where requests fell through to fallback routing, causing heavier-than-normal load on the fallback variant, which then hit OOMs on a small subset of hosts.
[01:05] Sara: yeah from our side we saw the same. a lot of requests started queueing at our ingress layer and we saw user errors in the client. we had to flip retries off to stop the client-side retry storm.
[01:20] Jordan: important note - Redwood automated fallback kicked in which prevented a full outage but the fallback model had lower QPS capacity for that hardware profile so latency stayed bad.
[01:30] Marcus: quick question — the canary rollback you mentioned, did that happen automatically per your rollout policy? who approved it?
[01:36] Priya: it was an automated rollback because the canary exceeded the failure threshold. the policy is set to 5% canary, 10 minute watch with a p95/p99 threshold. the immediate rollback is automated, though an oncall can override. in this case the automation rolled it back before a manual intervention.
[01:55] Evan: was there any human in the loop after rollback that could have prevented the cache invalidation?
[02:00] Priya: our logs show that the upstream invalidation message was processed out of order in the rebalance handler during rollback state. that's the subtle bug we traced. manual intervention could have mitigated but the automation happened faster than ops could react.
[02:18] Alex: can you clarify "out of order"? like a race on the invalidation queue?
[02:22] Priya: yeah race between invalidate and reshard messages — the reshard applied before the invalidation marker in certain sequences, leaving stale pointers for some keys.
[02:35] Tina: from a product POV this manifested as degraded chat suggestions and some NLU failures for a subset of users, we saw increased support tickets.
[02:48] Jordan: okay can we walk through mitigations you applied Friday and what we pushed overnight? Luis?
[02:52] Luis (CSM): quick call at 02:40 with Lyra SRE and Redwood SEs. we rolled a hotfix to force-consistent invalidation and disabled automatic canary rollback temporarily for the critical route while we validated the hotfix. That stabilized cache consistency by 03:30 UTC and latency gradually returned to baseline by 04:20.
[03:18] Sara: confirmation - after hotfix we still saw a small tail of errors for about 40 minutes due to drained connections on older hosts. cleaned up by 05:05.
[03:32] Marcus: were any logs or PII exposed during the event? that's our top security concern.
[03:36] Priya: no evidence of PII exfiltration; the failure was within cache pointers and routing metadata, not payload storage. we captured full audit logs and will share a sanitized extract.
[03:48] Marcus: we need that extract for our audit; SOC2 team will want to see it.
[03:51] Jordan: we'll get that to you. Priya you'll run export?
[03:54] Priya: yes, I'll produce the canary rollback traces and the invalidation queue dump.
[04:00] Evan: thanks. now longer-term — curious what you're recommending to avoid recurrence.
[04:05] Priya: we have three tiers: immediate, short-term, and long-term. immediate is the hotfix we pushed. short-term is adjust canary policy and add guard rails: increase canary to 10% for this route and add a delayed rollback path requiring 1 human ack for critical routes during major changes. add pre-rollback validation that checks queue ordering.
[04:30] Jordan: long-term we recommend: improved observability on invalidate/reshard sequences, introduce a transactional invalidation protocol (two-phase) for the KV layer, and offer a Dedicated capacity pilot for Lyra’s critical chat endpoints so you have predictable isolates and we can stage canaries there without shared cluster risk.
[04:57] Tina: Dedicated sounds promising but cost is a concern — can you ballpark?
[05:02] Jordan: yes we'll provide a 30/60/90 day pilot estimate with committed throughput tiers. we'll couple that with model quantization and batching config to offset cost.
[05:16] Alex: curious operationally — with Dedicated would we still have the same automated rollout flows?
[05:22] Priya: yes same Redwood Console features, but you gain isolated GPU pools and stronger failure isolation. we can configure more conservative rollout policies for Dedicated.
[05:31] Marcus: on the compliance side, after the event our audit wants evidence that rollback automation respects escalation policies and is logged. do you have immutable audit logs / KMS evidence?
[05:44] Priya: the control plane logs all rollout events, signed with KMS-backed key IDs. we can provide the audit trail; some of the most detailed traces live in the private control plane for Dedicated, but we exported what we have for hosted.
[05:58] Marcus: okay we need the KMS key IDs and the signed event sample to associate with our SOC2 evidence.
[06:05] Jordan: noted — Priya will include that in the export.
[06:10] Evan: one thing we flagged internally — client retry behavior exacerbated the load. we had a retry storm. any recommendations?
[06:18] Priya: yes implement client-side exponential backoff and jitter plus circuit-breaker for 5xx spikes. Redwood can provide a recommended SDK update that enforces sensible defaults for retries.
[06:34] Tina: did the fallback model cause data residency or compliance changes? we were worried about model telemetry going to a different pool.
[06:42] Priya: fallback stayed in same region, same data handling rules. only the model variant changed (smaller param count); no telemetry was redirected off-region.
[06:52] Alex: can we see the traffic heatmap that led to OOMs? specific time windows?
[06:58] Jordan: we'll include a CSV of request rates and memory pressure per host.
[07:02] Sara: we also want to run a tabletop exercise simulating a canary rollback leading to cache rekeying — ideally run it before you change canary thresholds.
[07:12] Luis: good call — joint tabletop test. we'll schedule it.
[07:16] Evan: what about adding SLO alerting tied to canary metrics? like if canary p99 deviates from baseline by X% send immediate page.
[07:25] Priya: we can instrument that; Redwood Console already supports per-route SLO alerts and can trigger webhooks to your PagerDuty. we can propose thresholds.
[07:34] Marcus: security request: can you include in the export the signed KMS IDs and encryption algorithms used for the audit trail?
[07:42] Priya: yes AES-256-GCM with KMS v2 signing; we'll include key IDs and signature samples.
[07:48] Tina: before we wrap — any immediate mitigations left undone?
[07:52] Priya: we've already disabled automatic rollback for that critical route in hosted temporarily; we've backfilled consistency checks and we've deployed a canary queue-order validator in staging. we recommend waiting for the bench and tabletop before re-enabling automatic rollback.
[08:10] Jordan: ok let's recap action items and owners. Priya will share exports and config. Jordan will do Dedicated sizing. Alex will share traffic patterns. Evan and Jordan will set benchmark window.
[08:25] Evan: timeline on the benchmark?
[08:28] Jordan: target week of 11/22; will confirm in email but we aim for a Wednesday run.
[08:34] Marcus: last ask — can Redwood include alternate rollback strategies as part of the proposal? like staged fallback (use model variant with same memory profile) rather than smaller models.
[08:44] Priya: yes we'll include multiple rollback strategies and cost tradeoffs.
[08:50] Tina: thanks all.
[08:51] Jordan: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with notes and links.
[08:55] Luis: thanks; end of call.

Post-call notes (auto):
- Root cause: race in invalidate/reshard ordering triggered by automated canary rollback.
- Mitigation applied: forced-consistent invalidation hotfix, temporary disable of auto-rollback on critical route, drained hosts cleanup.
- Short-term improvements: increase canary to 10% for critical route, require human ack for rollback on critical routes, add pre-rollback queue-order validation, SDK retry defaults with jitter.
- Long-term improvements: two-phase transactional invalidation protocol, enhanced per-key observability and tracing, Dedicated capacity pilot option for critical endpoints, improved rollback strategies and staging for model variants.
